subject: Decision follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated for latency-sensitive payments workflow
messages:

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Decision follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated for latency-sensitive payments workflow

Hi Oliver / Sofia —

Thanks again for your time on the call earlier. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we all stay aligned: 

Summary of FinPay requirements (as discussed):
- Use case: real-time fraud scoring and authorization decisioning in the payments path
- Typical inference model: distilled open LLM + downstream scoring logic
- Performance targets: p95 inference latency (end-to-end) target < 150 ms
- Traffic profile: steady-state ~300–500 QPS, with short bursts up to ~800 QPS (30–60s) during peak times
- Availability requirement: 99.9% SLA (would like 99.95% if possible)
- Data concerns: PII in requests, standard SOC2/compliance questions (you already shared the questionnaire)

Options we discussed: Hosted API (fast onboarding, pay-as-you-go) vs Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput) vs Private VPC (for stricter network/data controls).

Next steps we agreed:
1) Dylan to share latency/throughput guidance + recommended sizing for Hosted vs Dedicated.
2) We’ll propose a short performance PoC to validate p95 at burst loads and confirm SLO feasibility.
3) Redwood to send a preliminary proposal and timeline (pricing ballpark + PoC plan).

I attached the requirements sheet you shared — I’ve added a tab with the call notes.

Thanks — I’ll follow up once Dylan sends the sizing details.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Subject: Re: Decision follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated for latency-sensitive payments workflow

Thanks Neha — good notes. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The p95 <150 ms target is for end-to-end inference (client->Redwood->client). We understand network adds some overhead; our target assumes a ~20–30 ms network budget.
- Bursts can spike to ~800 QPS but are short (typically 20–60s). It's important that we avoid sustained throttling during those spikes — degraded latency or queueing causes downstream declines in authorization throughput.
- Cost is a factor: if Dedicated gives us consistent latency but at 2–3x hosted cost, we need to see the business case.

Could Dylan share:
1) Typical p95 numbers for Hosted vs Dedicated (for models ~7B–13B), including variability during short bursts.
2) Recommended Dedicated sizing (GPU type / number of replicas) to handle steady-state + burst headroom without significant queuing.
3) A proposed PoC plan (duration, success criteria, data needed).

If you can get that over this week, we can take to our infra leads and loop back on a proposed start date.

—Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Platform Engineering | FinPay
oliver@finpay.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@finpay.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-21T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Decision follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated for latency-sensitive payments workflow

Oliver —

Thanks for the clarifications. Below is a pragmatic sizing and recommendation based on the traffic profile and latency SLO you shared. I’ll keep things high-level but can provide a detailed runbook if you want to proceed to a PoC.

Quick definitions:
- p95: 95th percentile server-side inference latency (excludes client network).
- Hosted API: multi-tenant Redwood endpoints with autoscaling; lower setup friction but some variability during system-wide bursts.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pool (customer-dedicated machines/pods) with predictable performance and configurable autoscale/burst behavior.

Measured guidance (7B–13B class models, optimized weights):
- Hosted (recommended model family): typical p95 = 120–250 ms (region-dependent). Under short bursty load, p95 can degrade to 200–350 ms unless we enable burst capacity or routing to additional regions.
- Dedicated (A100 / H100 class nodes, tuned runtime, quantized): typical p95 = 70–130 ms. With extra caching (prefix/KV) and model distillation/quantization, we regularly see 50–80 ms p95 for highly optimized paths.

Throughput considerations:
- Batching increases tokens/sec but also increases tail latency. For your use-case (strict p95), we’ll prioritize schedulers that favor low single-request latency over maximum batch throughput.
- For sustained 300–500 QPS with 800 QPS short bursts, a conservative Dedicated sizing is: 4 reserved A100-equivalent replicas with an autoscale policy to add 2 more replicas when traffic >650 QPS for >15s. This gives headroom to absorb 800 QPS spikes with minimal queuing.

Tradeoffs / recommendation:
- If you need consistent p95 <150 ms under spikes, Dedicated is the safer bet. Hosted can meet the target most of the time but has higher variance during platform-wide events or cold starts.
- Cost: Dedicated will be ~1.5–2.5x higher monthly than Hosted for the reserved capacity above (exact depends on commitment term and region). We can model exact pricing in the proposal.

Proposed PoC (two-week technical validation):
- Duration: 2 weeks (1 week warm / soak, 3 days of controlled spike testing, final 2–3 days for tuning and report).
- Success criteria: p95 observed <= 150 ms for 95% of test windows during controlled 800 QPS spikes; no more than 1% error rate; acceptable CPU/GPU utilization without OOM throttles.
- What we need from FinPay: representative traffic profiles (sample request traces or synthetic generator), model artifact or model spec (tokenization + average prompt length), and a contact for network whitelisting and test orchestration.

I’ve attached a sizing workbook that translates QPS -> GPU count for a few typical models. If you’re aligned, we can schedule the PoC to start the week of July 5th. I’ll also prepare a draft proposal with cost ranges for Hosted vs Dedicated and a suggested commitment structure for Dedicated.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_hosted_vs_dedicated_sizing.xlsx
